Meqabyan (Ethiopian tradition) First Book of Meqabyan (Mäṣḥafä Mäqabyan I) (c. 600 AD)

FOUR-KINGDOMS APOCALYPSE — the most internally diagnostic chapter in 1 Mq for dating and provenance. Opening verses lay out a sequence of kingdom-pairings climaxing in an extraordinary claim about kingdom-establishment-over-kingdom. The four-kingdoms schema is parallel to Daniel 2 + Daniel 7 (the Babylon-Persia-Greece-Rome succession), but Meqabyan's specific ethnographic list — Judah + Cyprus + Samaria + Damascus + Babylon + India + Nubia + Sheba + Egypt + Ethiopia — extends the Danielic horizon INTO THE EAST (India + Sheba + Ethiopia) in a way distinctive to Ethiopian-Christian-apocalyptic. The chapter also contains a Nebuchadnezzar-to-Daniel citation about 'the spirit of God upon you' (Dan 5:14 echo), locating the apocalypse-genre within the Danielic tradition.

Meqabyan (Ethiopian tradition) First Book of Meqabyan (Mäṣḥafä Mäqabyan I) (c. 600 AD)

NEBUCHADNEZZAR-TO-DANIEL citation: 'the SPIRIT OF GOD UPON YOU' — direct echo of DANIEL 5:14 (Belshazzar to Daniel: 'I have even heard of thee, that the spirit of the gods is in thee, and that light and understanding and excellent wisdom is found in thee') + DANIEL 4:8-9 (Nebuchadnezzar to Daniel: 'in whom is the spirit of the holy gods... thou canst; for the spirit of the holy gods is in thee'). The Danielic spirit-of-God-upon-the-prophet vocabulary locates Meqabyan within the DANIELIC PROPHETIC-INSPIRATION tradition. The chapter's broader four-kingdoms apocalypse (seed 34:1) extends the Danielic apocalyptic-framework INTO THE ETHIOPIAN HORIZON via the chapter's eastward-toponym extensions. The Spirit-upon-the-prophet vocabulary is itself a CHRISTOLOGICAL-PNEUMATOLOGICAL anchor: Luke 4:18 (Christ at Nazareth: 'the Spirit of the Lord is upon me') applies Isaiah 61:1's same vocabulary to himself. Tewahedo Christology preserves the Spirit-upon-the-prophet pattern as prefiguring Christ's-anointing.
